reason: The text actually contradicts this statement. God explicitly acknowledges and validates the Israelites' cries and complaints: 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry' (וְאֶת־ צַעֲקָתָ֤ם שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙). God responds positively to their complaints by committing to their liberation. The narrative's moral concerns God's covenant, compassion, and redemptive action—not the suppression of complaints. Rather, it demonstrates that God hears and responds to the suffering and voices of the oppressed.
